claims.title: Sensitive-path docs now bypass review when small, including non-prose doc extensions
claims.text:
🟢 **P3** · advisory

**Sensitive-path docs now bypass review when small, including non-prose doc extensions**

The doc-only trivial check now runs before isSensitivePath, so any <20-line change to files with a DOC_EXTENSIONS extension skips the sensitive check. This is intended for .md. If DOC_EXTENSIONS also includes extensions like .txt or .rst (not visible in the diff), a small edit to a sensitive-named file such as secrets.txt or auth/allowlist.txt would now be trivial. The requirements/constraints carve-out only covers two names, so it is a narrow special case rather than a general rule. Consider restricting the early-trivial path to prose doc extensions.

<!-- ai-review:fp=architecture|src/router.ts|46bea9eacfe8aab1.0 -->
<!-- ai-review:advisory -->

claims.title: Doc ordering: isDocFile defined after isTrivialDoc and sensitive .txt logic relies on extension slice
claims.text:
🟢 **P3** · advisory

**Doc ordering: isDocFile defined after isTrivialDoc and sensitive .txt logic relies on extension slice**

When a path has no "." (e.g. `docs/LICENSE`), `lastIndexOf(".")` returns -1 and `slice(-1)` yields the last character of the path, which is harmless here but fragile. More importantly, a dotfile or a dot in a directory name (e.g. `docs.v2/README`) yields an extension like `.v2/README`, so the prose check is skipped and the sensitive-path fallback applies. Consider using the basename when computing the extension.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
	const base = path.slice(path.lastIndexOf("/") + 1);
	const dot = base.lastIndexOf(".");
	const ext = dot === -1 ? "" : base.slice(dot).toLowerCase();
```

<!-- ai-review:fp=nitpick|src/router.ts|07f397df81f0a14e.0 -->
<!-- ai-review:sfp=46ffb44ca888abdd -->
<!-- ai-review:advisory -->

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Fixed in 2c60112c. A small sensitive-named .txt now falls through to the sensitive check and routes complex; only .md, .mdx and .rst count as prose docs for the trivial shortcut. Tests cover secrets.txt and auth/allowlist.txt.

replies.author: joeblackwaslike
replies.body: Hardened in 7ffceca1 by taking the extension from the basename. The failure described does not occur with today's extension sets, since .v2/README and a single trailing character match no entry in DOC_EXTENSIONS, so behaviour is unchanged and the new tests (docs.v2/README, docs/LICENSE, auth.v2/LICENSE, docs.v2/guide.md) pass before and after. Rating this as a fragility note, not a bug.
